scope.method: count ladder with tiny images first, then single-image climb, then squeeze-to-exact; JSON body bytes
conventions: Sizes are JSON request-body bytes, reported in binary units (MiB = 1024^2).
A bracket is written 'largest accepted - first failure'; it is not a precise cap unless the squeeze run resolved one.
A row with no byte wall found is a LOWER BOUND on that host, never 'unlimited'.
'largest accepted' means HTTP 200 with max_tokens=1, one model per host, one region, one key tier.
Structural caps (item counts, token budgets) bind before bytes on several hosts; the byte wall is then unreachable rather than absent.
Values are JSON request-body bytes in binary units (MiB = 1024^2).
kind=resolved_cap: a squeeze run resolved the exact ceiling.
kind=stated_in_error: the cap parsed out of the vendor's own rejection text.
kind=accepted_max: the largest request these probes saw accepted — exceeding it is unmeasured territory, not a proven failure.
One model per provider, one region, one key tier: a row is a dated sample, not a spec.

_comment: Maps a Hermes provider name onto a payload-walls provider id.
'region_mismatch' means the row was measured on the international host, so the CN/self-hosted
endpoint may differ. Providers absent from this file are reported as 'no measured row' rather

Keys are Hermes' canonical provider ids: a name with no key here is reported as 'no measured row' (UNKNOWN) and never as inside a ceiling. openrouter and github-copilot have no measured row in the dataset.

openai.label: OpenAI

image_total_bytes.note: '50MB' read as decimal. The measured pair — 17 x 2,053,887 B accepted, 18 x the same rejected with 'Total image size is 50.56MB, which exceeds the allowed limit of 50MB' — is reproduced by 50,000,000 against base64 bytes x 1.0257, and NOT by a 50 MiB reading. The vendor counts its own normalised copy, so a few very large images (8 x 12,144,445 B, accepted) pass far above this budget: those are downscaled before counting. Expect a false positive on that shape; the plugin records it.

openai.notes: Two payload shapes probed. (a) many-small: 17 x 2,053,887 B accepted, 18 rejected at 400 'Total image size is 50.56MB, which exceeds the allowed limit of 50MB.' (b) few-large: 8 x 12,144,448 B accepted (raw 97,155,560 B, body 129,541,440 B) - a 3.5x larger payload than the rejected small-image one. Rejection is HTTP 400, not 413.
openai.documented: Request size: Up to 512 MB total payload per request. Image count: Up to 1,500 images per request.

alibaba.label: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (DashScope international)

items.note: DashScope says 'data-uri' rather than 'image'; Hermes' own classifier misses this wording

item_bytes.note: vendor wording is 'Maximum single Base64 content: 20 MiB'; the failing rung sent 20.3 MiB decoded (27 MiB encoded) so both readings fit the observation — encoded is the stricter one, and the 96-image 512 MiB run that passed stayed far below it

alibaba.notes: 200 items / 267,075,137 B body accepted. The 250-item bracket completed: 400 'Exceeded limit on max data-uri per request: 250'. Free-tier credit was exhausted during the final rung, so the last rung is structural-cap evidence, not a byte measurement.
alibaba.documented: Requests without Base64: body max 16 MiB. Requests with Base64 (Anthropic protocol): single Base64 item max 32 MiB. Requests with Base64 (other protocols): single Base64 item max 20 MiB. Requests with Base64 (whole body): max 64 MiB. After server-side decoding the whole body must still not exceed 16 MiB; exceeding the limit is rejected by the gateway with HTTP 413.

gemini.label: Google Gemini API (AI Studio)

input_tokens.note: token budget, not a byte wall; counts depend on image resolution

gemini.notes: Earlier apparent ceilings on this host were per-model quota (429) and transient 503 ('high demand'), not payload size - retries resolved both. No byte cap found to 324 MiB.
gemini.documented: Inline data: 100 MB per request or payload (50 MB for PDFs). File API upload: 2 GB per file, up to 20 GB per project.

fireworks.label: Fireworks AI
fireworks.notes: The 60-image rejection string is already public: browser-use/browsercode#127 (merged 2026-07-30). Non-conformance is with the vendor's own docs.
fireworks.documented: 30 images maximum per request; the total base64-encoded images must be less than 10MB.

anthropic.label: Anthropic
anthropic.notes: An earlier circulating '5 MB per image' figure is the Bedrock/Vertex/consumer-app number, not the direct API. Rejection is 413 request_too_large.
anthropic.documented: Request size: 32 MB for the Messages API (256 MB Batches, 500 MB Files). Per image: 10 MB base64 on the direct API (5 MB on Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud).

deepseek.label: DeepSeek
deepseek.notes: 413 from openresty: 'Failed to buffer the request body: length limit exceeded'. Vision is live on the direct API although /models lists no vision id.
deepseek.documented: Request body 48 MiB; image file size limit 32 MB; up to 600 images.

zai.label: Z.ai (GLM)
zai.notes: Wording ('exceeds the limit') matches the pattern clients use to detect context overflow, so an oversize body here can be misclassified as a token problem. No CDN in front (Alibaba Cloud IPs).
zai.documented: No numeric request-size figure located on the vendor's error-code page.

kimi-coding.label: Moonshot AI (Kimi)
kimi-coding.notes: RPM 3 on this key - space the rungs. Live model id kimi-k3 (kimi-k2-turbo-preview 404s).

minimax.label: MiniMax
minimax.notes: Probed over the Anthropic-compatible wire. A PAYG (sk-api-) key returns 402 insufficient balance; the subscription key works.
minimax.documented: No numeric body-cap figure located; error-code page lists the 413 wording only.

deepinfra.label: DeepInfra
deepinfra.notes: Served by uvicorn, no CDN. The 500 is the interesting part: a client retrying 5xx will loop on a request that can never succeed.
deepinfra.documented: No numeric request-size figure located; rate-limit page documents concurrency only.

novita.label: Novita AI
novita.notes: Cloudflare-fronted. Origin is slow: 199 s to answer a 50 MiB body - latency, not rejection; use a long client timeout or the wall looks smaller than it is.
novita.documented: Error catalogue lists INVALID_REQUEST_BODY and IMAGE_FILE_EXCEEDS_MAX_SIZE without numeric ceilings.

nvidia.label: NVIDIA NIM (integrate.api.nvidia.com)

body_bytes.note: 25 MiB exact, stated in the error text

nvidia.notes: The same 25 MiB string is quoted in NousResearch/hermes-agent#112473 - that is this project's own prior slice, not independent prior art.
nvidia.documented: No numeric request-size figure located in the API reference.

ollama-cloud.label: Ollama Cloud

body_bytes.note: bracket only (15.9-16.5 MiB) — the cap is not exact

ollama-cloud.notes: The measured 16 MiB coincides with a common framework default request-body guard, so the wall may be infrastructure rather than a published product limit.
ollama-cloud.documented: No numeric payload figure located; the pricing page documents plan tiers only.

gmi.label: GMI Cloud
gmi.notes: Ambiguous row: the first failure is plausibly the CDN, so the origin ceiling is unestablished above 40.5 MiB.
gmi.documented: Rate-limit page documents RPM/TPM and concurrency, no body ceiling.

nebius-token-factory.label: Nebius Token Factory
nebius-token-factory.notes: An oversize image returns HTTP 400 with a pydantic message - 'Input should be a valid string' on messages[0].content - not a 413, so 413-keyed recovery never fires here.

upstage.label: Upstage

items.note: the measured endpoint rejects image input outright ('Image input is not allowed for this model')

upstage.notes: No vision on the chat endpoint at all - a capability gap, not a limit.
upstage.documented: Images are handled by separate products (Document Parse / Document OCR / Information Extraction), not by the chat endpoint.

xai.label: xAI

item_bytes.note: documented-only row: no API key on the measuring host, so this is NOT verified here

xai.notes: Documented-only row. Do not treat the 25 MB as measured.
xai.documented: Per-image limit 20 MiB documented; Batch API states 25 MB per request. No chat-body ceiling published.

openai-codex.label: OpenAI Codex backend (ChatGPT)
openai-codex.notes: Included to record that the gap is a quota artefact. Note also that this backend silently falls back to a different provider on some client configurations, so a success here must be verified by reading the response's provider field, not the output text.
openai-codex.documented: No published payload ceiling for this private backend.

copilot.label: GitHub Copilot API
copilot.notes: Recorded as an observed-413 row with no measurement. Hermes aliases github-models onto this id, which is a different host and tier.

alibaba-token-plan.label: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (token-plan endpoint)
alibaba-token-plan.notes: Unmeasured. Variant endpoint; the same key 401s here.
alibaba-token-plan.documented: No published payload ceiling for this endpoint variant.
